title: Notes for a Community Exhibition
paragraphs: The community center was planning an exhibition about everyday experiences. Students volunteered to select the written material. Their challenge was to find a balance between vivid individual moments and a larger theme that visitors could follow without already knowing the people involved.

The first section of the collection placed these observations side by side. Through the fog, we could barely discern the shape of the lighthouse. The bright collar helps us distinguish our dog from the others. Without counting every seat, we can estimate the hall's capacity. The judges will evaluate each design using the same standards.

A later section added further scenes for comparison. From her muddy boots, I could infer that she had crossed the field. The guide helped us interpret the symbols on the ancient wall. Detectives will investigate the disappearance by interviewing the witnesses. You must justify your conclusion with evidence from the passage.

By the end of the discussion, the students had learned why careful reading requires more than a quick judgment. A useful interpretation must fit the details of the situation. They chose a conclusion that acknowledged differences among the accounts, and they left readers with a question: which observation most strongly supports your view, and what might change your mind?

targets.definition: to recognize something not easily noticed
to recognize a difference between things
to judge the worth or quality of
to reach a conclusion from clues
to examine in order to discover facts
to provide a good reason for
